query: What travel policy risks appear in expense descriptions?

per_column.name: asset_category_type
per_column.rationale: Categorizing the CI asset is a reasonable axis, but it is largely redundant with the ci field and only tangential to TRAVEL POLICY risk. Groundedness is undermined by clear miscategorisation: 'Dell OptiPlex 7070 Desktop' labeled 'laptop', contradicting the source text.

per_column.name: travel_equipment_marker
per_column.rationale: A travel-equipment flag is directly relevant to the travel-policy query and gives a groupable axis. However none of the sampled rows (all hardware/cloud) support inferring travel status, and it is partly redundant with asset_category_type's travel buckets; groundedness for silent rows is uncertain.

per_column.name: expense_automation_method
per_column.rationale: Automatic vs manual entry is weakly connected to travel policy risk. It is derivable from phrasing ('Automated creation' -> automatic_generation; 'Procurement' -> manual_entry) so grounding is fair, but the three-way split (automatic_generation vs automated_entry) looks arbitrary and the analytical leverage for THIS query is low.

per_column.name: receipt_or_approval_risk
per_column.rationale: Receipt/approval requirements are a plausible policy-risk axis, but these values appear invented: nothing in the source rows states receipt or approval requirements. Assigning 'receipt_required'/'approval_required' confidently to silent hardware descriptions is unwarranted assertion.

per_column.name: personal_use_risk_indicator
per_column.rationale: Personal-use risk is squarely relevant to travel policy. But the source texts (procurement of hardware) give no basis for a personal-use inference; 146 'true' assignments are not supported by anything in the sampled evidence, suggesting fabricated signal.

per_column.name: department_compliance_context
per_column.rationale: This is essentially a restatement of the existing 'department' column, adding little analytical leverage. Values may or may not match the original department field; the label 'compliance_context' overstates content that is just a department copy.

per_column.name: ci_vendor_brand
per_column.rationale: Vendor extracted from the ci string (Dell, AWS, HP) is well grounded and can support spend-by-vendor grouping, but it is largely redundant with ci and only loosely tied to travel-policy risk.

per_column.name: high_value_risk_flag
per_column.rationale: A high-value flag is a useful risk axis and the original 'amount' column could ground it. However the threshold basis is unstated and none of the sampled rows expose amount to verify the True assignments, leaving grounding partly unverifiable.

per_column.name: miscellaneous_or_undefined_asset
per_column.rationale: Largely redundant with asset_category_type (the 'miscellaneous' bucket) and near-inverse of other flags; adds little new leverage for travel-policy analysis. Grounding is inconsistent given asset_category_type miscategorisations.

judge.rationale: Several columns offer genuine travel-policy-risk axes (travel_equipment_marker, personal_use_risk_indicator, high_value_risk_flag), but a large share are redundant restatements of existing fields (department_compliance_context ~ department; ci_vendor_brand, asset_category_type, miscellaneous_or_undefined_asset ~ ci) or only tangential to the query. Groundedness is the bigger concern: sampled rows show a clear misclassification (a Desktop labeled 'laptop') and, more seriously, policy-risk columns (receipt_or_approval_risk, personal_use_risk_indicator) assert confident specifics that the source text does not support, indicating fabricated signal rather than warranted inference.
